content:
- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (positive sentiment > 0.20) — model tends to overshoot early rallies.
- Underestimate prices in bearish sentiment (negative sentiment < -0.30) — model fails to capture sharp declines or mean reversion.
- Lagged price movements are often over-predicted — model reacts too slowly to sentiment shifts, especially after -0.40 sentiment.
- After a spike (e.g., >70), model often overcorrects downward, underestimating the continuation or reversal.
- Mean reversion bias: model assumes prices return to prior 10-15 day average too quickly, ignoring sentiment-driven momentum.
- Sentiment reversal (e.g., from +0.30 to -0.30) triggers model to overcorrect — forecast drops too fast, missing sustained trend.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts are overly sensitive to recent sentiment spikes — model overweights short-term sentiment over longer-term trends.
